written: 2026-09-25 by Claude Opus 5.5 from snapshot chunk text only, before any retrieval or rerank result existed for these queries
method: Seeded candidates from families.py (seed capy-rerank-20260925) over the frozen 43-book snapshot, walked in order: samedoc candidates 0-79 of 128, nearmiss candidates 0-46 of 129. Each accepted candidate got one learner question or study request answered by the target chunk but not by its look-alike siblings (samedoc) or its nominated neighbours (nearmiss); skips are listed with reasons. Query language was pre-assigned per candidate by the seeded rule in families.py (about one in five non-English) before the candidate was read. samedoc subtype 'locator' names a printed item (Figure 8.10, Example 101, Guided Practice 1.36, Exercise 2.5.5); 'content' describes the item. Distractors are the look-alikes that do not answer; they are recorded for error classification and are never scored.

cohorts.samedoc: same-document competition: the answer is one chunk among look-alike siblings in a long book (numbered items, exercise lists, parallel subsections)
cohorts.nearmiss: near-miss distractor: a closely related passage exists that answers a different task, condition, number, level or concept

relevance: relevant = target + acceptable (chunks that answer the question equally, including the same passage in a fork book such as os4/ahss4 or the R and jamovi editions, and continuation chunks of the same item). Every near-copy of a target (char 5-gram Jaccard >= 0.6 or containment >= 0.8, the qwen3.7 rule) carries an explicit acceptable/not_acceptable decision made at freeze. relevant_excerpts = excerpts holding a relevant chunk; excerpt level is primary, as search_knowledge returns excerpts. Look-alikes inside the target's own excerpt are listed under same_excerpt_siblings: excerpt-level scoring cannot separate them from the target, so they only bear on the chunk-level (displayed hit chunk) metric.
